346858.title: Non-constant-solution nonexistence conjecture for the tEoM on $T_2$
346858.statement: Let $T_2$ be the graph appearing in the paper, and let a setting be an assignment of edge lengths satisfying the tEoM. The **non-constant-solution nonexistence conjecture** states that there exists no non-constant solution to the tEoM on $T_2$ when all edge lengths are positive. This is the second conjecture in the paper's discussion of positive solutions and remains unproved in the supplied text.

346999.title: Nonnegative tensor-power conjecture for homology of rank-selected subword order
346999.statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet of size $n\ge 2$, and let $S_n$ act on $A^*$ by permuting the alphabet. A **rank-selected subposet** is obtained by retaining words whose ranks belong to a finite nonempty set. Let $S_{(n-1,1)}$ be the irreducible representation indexed by the partition $(n-1,1)$. **Nonnegative tensor-power conjecture.** The $S_n$-action on the homology of any finite nonempty rank-selected subposet of subword order on $A^*$ is a nonnegative integer combination of positive tensor powers of $S_{(n-1,1)}$.

347000.title: Almost h-positivity conjecture for rank-selected subword-order homology
347000.statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet of size $n\ge 2$, and let $S_n$ act on $A^*$ by permuting the alphabet. A **rank-selected subposet** is obtained by retaining words whose ranks belong to a finite nonempty set. Let $S_{(n-1,1)}$ be the reflection representation of $S_n$, and set $T_2(n)=\{h_\lambda: \lambda=(n-r,1^r),\ r\ge 2\}$. **Almost h-positivity conjecture.** The homology of any finite nonempty rank-selected subposet of subword order on $A^*$, plus or minus one copy of $S_{(n-1,1)}$, is a permutation module. Its Frobenius characteristic is $h$-positive and supported on $T_2(n)$.

347099.title: The central Delannoy formula for subdivisions of a 2 × n grid
347099.statement:
Let an $m\times n$ grid be the point configuration consisting of the lattice points in an $m\times n$ rectangular grid, and let a **subdivision** be a subdivision of this point configuration. For $n\geq 2$, denote by $D_{n-1}$ the $(n-1)$th central Delannoy number.

**Central Delannoy formula.** The number of subdivisions of a $2\times n$ grid is

$$
2^{n-2}D_{n-1}.
$$

The conjecture proposes a closed formula for the total number of subdivisions of a $2\times n$ grid, extending the small cases computed in the paper. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

347122.title: Real spectral-radius eigenvalue conjecture for ALS on canonical tensor decomposition
347122.statement:
Let $q$ be the ALS fixed-point map for canonical tensor decomposition, and let $x^*$ be a fixed point. Write $q'$ for the Jacobian evaluated at $x^*$, and let $\rho_{q'}$ denote its spectral radius after excluding the eigenvalues equal to $1$ caused by Hessian degeneracy at $x^*$. **Real spectral-radius eigenvalue conjecture.** There exists a real eigenvalue $\mu$ of $q'$ such that

$$
\rho_{q'}=\mu.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by numerical tests for ALS on canonical tensor decomposition; the cited work indicates that the relevant spectral-radius condition is known for ALS, while its general validity in this setting remains a topic for further research.

347230.title: The kernel conjecture for the second-kind interval transform
347230.statement:
Let ${\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$ denote the vector space of homogeneous noncommutative $ab$-polynomials of degree $n$, and let $I_2:{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n\rightarrow {\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_{n+1}$ be the interval transform of the second kind. Let $A_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$ be the specified subspace of ${\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$. 

**Kernel conjecture.** For each $n\geq 1$, 

$$
\ker I_2=A_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n.
$$

The conjecture identifies precisely the kernel of the second-kind interval transform, whose nontrivial kernel distinguishes it from the corresponding Tchebyshev operator framework. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

347231.title: The eigenvector generation conjecture for the second-kind interval transform
347231.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Pyr}:u\mapsto M(1,u)$ be the pyramid operator, let ${\mathcal L}$ be the lift operator sending $u$ to $(a-b)u$, and let $S_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$ denote the specified degree-$n$ subspace of homogeneous $ab$-polynomials. 

**Eigenvector generation conjecture.** For each $n\geq 1$, a generating set of $S_{\mathbb Q}\langle a,b\rangle_n$, consisting only of eigenvectors, may be obtained by applying all possible $n$-fold compositions of $\operatorname{Pyr}$ and ${\mathcal L}$ to $1$.

This conjecture proposes a complete eigenvector-based generation procedure for the relevant subspace, paralleling the construction used for the Tchebyshev operator of the second kind. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

347354.title: Kitaev and Zhang's Stieltjes continued fraction conjecture for mesh pattern 3
347354.statement:
For a pattern $p$ and a permutation $\pi$, let $p(\pi)$ denote the number of occurrences of $p$ in $\pi$. Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $y$ and $t$ be indeterminates. **Kitaev and Zhang's conjecture.** The bivariate generating function for occurrences of mesh pattern $3$ satisfies

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0}t^n \sum_{\pi\in S_n}y^{p(\pi)}=\cfrac{1}{1-\cfrac{\alpha_1t}{1-\cfrac{\alpha_2t}{1-\cdots}}}
$$

with coefficients

$$
\alpha_{2k-1}=k,\qquad \alpha_{2k}=y+k-1.
$$

This is a conjectured Stieltjes continued fraction formula for the distribution of mesh pattern 3; the supplied text attributes it to Kitaev and Zhang's Conjecture 6.1, and does not provide evidence of a resolution.

347468.title: Nine-weight conjecture for the subfield code associated with $x^6$
347468.statement:
Let $q=2^m$, and let ${\mathcal{C}}_{(f,q)}^{(2)}$ be the binary subfield code defined by the trace representation for an oval polynomial $f$. **Nine-weight conjecture.** For odd $m\geq 5$, the code ${\mathcal{C}}_{(x^6,q)}^{(2)}$ has parameters

$$
[2^m+1,2m,2^{m-1}-2^{(m-1)/2}],
$$

and nine nonzero weights. Its dual has parameters $[2^m+1,2^m-2m+1,3]$. The minimal distance and weight distribution were not determined in the paper, and this claim is based on Magma experiments.

347469.title: Nine-weight conjecture for the subfield code associated with the second oval polynomial
347469.statement:
Let $q=2^m$, with $m\equiv 3\pmod 4$ and $m\geq 5$, and define

$$
f(x)=x^{2^{(m+1)/2}+2^{(m+1)/4}}.
$$

Let ${\mathcal{C}}_{(f,q)}^{(2)}$ be the associated binary subfield code. **Nine-weight conjecture.** The code ${\mathcal{C}}_{(f,q)}^{(2)}$ has parameters

$$
[2^m+1,2m,2^{m-1}-2^{(m-1)/2}],
$$

and nine nonzero weights. Its dual has parameters $[2^m+1,2^m-2m+1,3]$. The claim is one of the conjectures prompted by Magma experiments because the minimal distance and weight distribution were not determined theoretically.

347731.title: The complexity trichotomy for circular-colouring mixing
347731.statement:
Let $G_{p,q}$ denote the graph used as the target for $(p,q)$-colourings, and let the textsc{G_{p,q}}-Mixing problem ask whether the reconfiguration graph of $(p,q)$-colourings of an input graph is connected. **Circular-colouring mixing complexity conjecture.** If

$$
\frac{p}{q}=2,
$$

then \textsc{G_{p,q}}-Mixing is in P; if

$$
2<\frac{p}{q}<4,
$$

then it is co-NP-complete; and if

$$
\frac{p}{q}\geq 4,
$$

then it is PSPACE-complete. The first two cases extend known complexity results for odd-cycle mixing and planar inputs, while the full classification remains open, particularly the PSPACE-completeness claim for ratios at least $4$.

347960.title: The bounded-color monochromatic-cover conjecture
347960.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$ and let $K$ be a complete graph whose edges are colored with colors in $[r]$. A **monochromatic cover** is a collection of monochromatic connected subgraphs covering all vertices, and its order is its number of subgraphs.

**Bounded-color cover conjecture.** Every such coloring has a monochromatic cover of order at most $r-1$ in which the subgraphs use at most $\lceil r/2\rceil$ distinct colors.

This is the balanced-subset special case of the S-versus-complement conjecture.

347972.title: The characterization of partitions with Schaper number at least three
347972.statement:
Let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition, and let $\nu_p(\lambda)$ denote its Schaper number. Suppose that $\lambda$ satisfies one of the conditions in the characterization referred to as `only if'.

**Schaper-number conjecture.** Then

$$
\nu_p(\lambda)\ge 3.
$$

Equivalently, the necessary conditions in that characterization are also sufficient, giving a complete characterization of partitions with Schaper number at least three. The conjecture concerns determining exactly when the Schaper number reaches at least three; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

347991.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the coupled Young graph dimension array
347991.statement:
Let $K(n,k,l)$ be the recursively defined array of integers associated with the pascalized coupled Young graph, with $n\geq 3$, $k,l$ satisfying $2k+l<n-2$ and $2k+l\equiv n\pmod 2$. **Monotonicity conjecture for $K$.** One has

$$
\frac{K(n-2,k,l)}{K(n,k,l)}\geq\max\left(\frac{K(n-2,k+1,l)}{K(n,k+1,l)},\frac{K(n-2,k,l+2)}{K(n,k,l+2)}\right).
$$

In particular,

$$
\max_{\substack{2k+l<n\\2k+l\equiv n\pmod 2}}\frac{K(n-2,k,l)}{K(n,k,l)}=\frac{K(n-2,0,\delta(n))}{K(n,0,\delta(n))},
$$

where $\delta(n)=0$ if $n$ is even and $\delta(n)=1$ if $n$ is odd. The paper reports verification for many cases but no proof, and presents this numerical claim as implying the preceding boundary-support conjecture.

348074.title: Fractional Albertson–Berman conjecture for planar graphs
348074.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $\fva(G)$ denote its fractional vertex-arboricity. **Fractional Albertson–Berman conjecture.** Every planar graph has fractional vertex-arboricity at most two, that is, 
$$
\fva(G)\leq 2.
$$
 This conjecture is a fractional analogue of the Albertson–Berman conjecture that every planar graph has an induced forest on at least half of its vertices. The paper notes that the best known general bound is $\fva(G)\leq 5/2$, and that the conjectured bound would imply the known upper bound four for the fractional chromatic number by a new method.

348106.title: The structure and substructure connectivity conjecture for hypercubes
348106.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, let $K_{1,r}$ be the star with $r$ leaves, and write $\kappa(Q_n;K_{1,r})$ and $\kappa^{s}(Q_n;K_{1,r})$ for the $K_{1,r}$-structure connectivity and $K_{1,r}$-substructure connectivity, respectively. **Hypercube connectivity conjecture.** For any integers $n\geq r\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$,

$$
\kappa(Q_{n};K_{1,r})=\kappa^{s}(Q_{n}; K_{1,r})=\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper proves this equality when $n>f(r)$, and also establishes it for $4\leq r\leq 6$ when $n\geq r$. The remaining cases identified in the paper are part of the open problem of determining star-structure connectivity for hypercubes.

348408.title: Cada et al.'s rainbow cycle length conjecture
348408.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored graph of order $n$, and let $k$ be a positive integer. For a vertex $v$ of $G$, write $d^c(v)$ for its color degree, the number of distinct edge colors incident with $v$. **Cada et al.'s conjecture.** If for each vertex $v$ of $G$, 
$$
d^c(v)>\frac{n+k}{2},
$$
 then $G$ contains a rainbow cycle of length at least $k$. This conjecture extends known results guaranteeing rainbow cycles under color-degree conditions; the supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.

348470.title: The unlabelled Diestel–Leader graph seeded tiling conjecture
348470.statement: For integers $p,q\geq 2$, let ${\mathsf{DL}(p,q)}$ be the Diestel–Leader graph, and let the **unlabelled graph** mean this graph considered without its standard edge labelling. A **seeded tiling problem** asks whether a finite tileset admits a tiling subject to a prescribed seed condition. **Unlabelled Diestel–Leader graph conjecture.** The unlabelled graph ${\mathsf{DL}(p,q)}$ has undecidable seeded tiling problem. The corresponding labelled Diestel–Leader graphs have undecidable seeded tiling problem, whereas the unlabelled case is posed as a better question and remains unresolved.

348613.title: The independent packing conjecture for regular symmetric bodies
348613.statement:
Let $C$ be a **regular symmetric body**, meaning a smooth, strictly convex centrally symmetric convex body in the plane that is not a linear transform of a disc. Let $G$ be a $(2,2)$-sparse graph.

**Independent packing conjecture.** There exists an independent $C$-packing with contact graph $G$.

This would be an analogue for regular symmetric bodies of the conjectured disc-packing result for $(2,3)$-sparse graphs. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

348627.title: Bannister–Oudot subdivision conjecture for stack-number
348627.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $k$ be an integer, and let $G'$ be any **$(\leqslant k)$-subdivision** of $G$, obtained by replacing each edge of $G$ by an internally disjoint path with at most $k$ internal vertices. Write $\operatorname{sn}(G)$ for the stack-number of $G$. **Bannister–Oudot subdivision conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sn}(G) \leqslant f(\operatorname{sn}(G'),k).
$$

The conjecture asserts that bounded-length subdivisions cannot reduce stack-number without a corresponding bound on the original graph's stack-number. The source states that a consequence of its construction resolves this conjecture, so the conjecture is solved.
